newsitem.title: USA: Clinton budget key to Los Angeles subway-authority.
newsitem.headline: Clinton budget key to Los Angeles subway-authority.

text.p: The Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority said on Thursday that funds earmarked by President Clinton for its projects would allow the agency to achieve its subway recovery plan.
Clinton earmarked $99 million for Los Angeles' Metro Rail construction program in his fiscal year 1998 budget.

If endorsed by Congress, this level of funding would enable the Los Angeles authority to achieve its Metro Red line subway recovery plan, which was adopted in January by the authority's board and submitted to the federal government.

"It is critical, however, that Congress appropriate the full amount ($99 million) if we are to stay on schedule," Metropolitan Transportation Authority Chairman Larry Zarian and Interim Chief Executive Linda Bohlinger said in a joint statement.

Faced with cost overruns and a projected $1 billion hole in Los Angeles County's long-range transportation budget, the authority's board of directors adopted a controversial plan last month to delay completion of two subway extension projects.
Under the recovery plan, the authority said it would need at least $100 million a year in federal funds to complete the projects on the revised schedule.
